clue.text: Admiralty body responsible for coast?

definitions.meaning: a board of the navy concerned with the sea, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a naval committee; as one it is the strip of land bordering the ocean.

clue.text: Got the betting odds on Yorkshire runner, mate?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: SP is short for starting price, the odds at which a horse starts
the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and a river runs

explanation.surface: A punter at the races checks the odds on a Yorkshire horse and asks a friend's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkshire runner' looks like a racehorse but is a river: the Ouse flows through York. SP (starting price) is the standard bookmakers' abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a partner in marriage, a husband or wife.

clue.text: Twin compositions of Gray about Beachy Head in wrangling dispute

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another, here a letter sits between the pair
twin says the piece that follows is used twice over
compositions are arrangements, so the letters of the name are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Two poems by Thomas Gray mention Beachy Head in some literary quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gray' is the poet Thomas Gray, but only his name's letters matter: 'compositions of' rearranges them, 'Twin' uses the result twice, and 'about' sets the Beachy Head letter between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Argy-bargy is British slang for a noisy quarrel or squabbling row.

clue.text: He has title, English worn out variety

indicators.note: out and variety both say the letters are mixed up into another form

explanation.surface: Someone notes that an English variety of something is worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out variety' rearranges E (English) and WORN together.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor holds legal title to his property.

clue.text: Sir Leo's chopped meat-ball

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters of the knight's name are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A knight named Leo chops up his meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of 'Sir Leo's' supplies a real letter: SIRLEOS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried patty or ball of minced meat.

clue.text: Swindle keeping Galatea in shape?

definitions.meaning: to cheat someone out of something
Galatea was the statue carved by Pygmalion, so a sculptor's tool kept her in shape

explanation.definitionFit: To cheat is slang for this verb, and a sculptor's cutting tool is what carved the statue Galatea.

clue.text: Parthian shot the object of cricket?

definitions.meaning: Parthian horsemen fired arrows while retreating, a strike followed by flight
the aim in cricket is to strike the ball and then score by running

explanation.definitionFit: A raid that strikes and flees is the Parthian tactic; in cricket the batsman strikes the ball and dashes between wickets.

clue.text: Fast writer

explanation.definitionFit: Speedy is a synonym, and the satirist of Gulliver's Travels bore the surname.

clue.text: Walker to finish �across lines of collected tales

parts.note: a leg is what one walks with
an end is a finish
RY, railway, gives railway lines

explanation.surface: A hiker reaches the finish across lines of stories gathered together.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) for 'lines' is a crossword convention; 'across' merely places the walker's finish against the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Legendry is a body of traditional stories gathered as one corpus.

clue.text: Arrange as orange is arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of the fruit and the little word are reordered

explanation.surface: A self-referential instruction: arrange it the way the fruit is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'arranged' twice: as the definition and as the anagram signal on ORANGE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To put in order is a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Train a number of racehorses

definitions.meaning: a train is a series or line of things following one another

explanation.definitionFit: A connected series is a synonym, and a trainer's stable of horses is called by the same name.

clue.text: Perhaps eastern part of church

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A guess about which end of the church a certain part lies in.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the rounded recess at a church's end, usually facing east, so it stands for the building by being part of it.

clue.text: Like one on bench-or not on at all

definitions.meaning: the saying 'as ___ as a judge' puts a judge on the bench
'on' is slang for tipsy, so not on at all means not drunk

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom compares a judge to the abstemious, and 'on' is slang for tipsy, so the opposite is clear-headed.

clue.text: Not poring over SE layer

indicators.note: over suggests the letters are turned over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told not to pore over a book again.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a hen: a layer of eggs bred at Orpington in south-east London, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed of laying hen takes its name from a town in south-east England.

clue.text: Gather iron will get it out

definitions.meaning: to gather fabric is to fold or pucker it
a fold or wrinkle in cloth is smoothed out by pressing

explanation.definitionFit: A fold in fabric is a pucker, and ironing smooths a wrinkle away.

clue.text: Are basalt components used in statue material?

indicators.note: components are parts put together, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A question about whether basalt rock goes into making sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white stone often carved into sculptures and ornaments.

clue.text: More' "lordy" further back?

definitions.meaning: lordy read as like a lord, an earl; more like one gives the comparative form

explanation.definitionFit: The comparative means more like a nobleman of that rank, and it also means previously.

clue.text: Cheek — nice one's going off about middle age

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters wrap round another piece
going off means spoiling or exploding, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: fifty is middle age, and L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone's cheekiness fading as they reach middle age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going off' rearranges NICE ONES; 'about' puts that round L, the Roman fifty, standing for 'middle age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek is impudence or rudeness.

clue.text: Flounder on board gets fare down

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship's letters

parts.note: aboard ship, SS standing for steamship
to flounder is to wallow

explanation.surface: A fish served on deck to a passenger who eats his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' looks like the fish but is the verb: WALLOW goes 'on board' SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: To get food down is to gulp it.

clue.text: Method set down when ambushed

parts.note: a way of doing things is a method
laid means placed or set down

explanation.surface: A method set down for how someone was ambushed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush is to lie in wait for and attack someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Bird dead, with nothing to follow it — you can say that again!

indicators.note: the exclamation tells us to repeat the pair
the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A bird is dead with nothing to follow, and someone agrees heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you can say that again' doubles D + O; the extinct bird is 'as dead as' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

clue.text: Unship violently and impose penalty

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Unloading a ship roughly and being fined for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflict a penalty is to discipline.

clue.text: Was it decorated with fly paper?

definitions.text: Was it decorated with fly paper?

parts.words: Was it decorated with fly paper?
parts.note: the spider's invitation in the rhyme, will you walk into my ___ said the spider to the fly, suggests a room lined for catching flies

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a sitting room had sticky fly-catcher strips on its walls.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'The Spider and the Fly' begins with the spider inviting the fly into this room.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a house, the room the spider offers to the fly.

clue.text: Top of pudding burning — his brandy is smuggled …

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

parts.note: arson is deliberate burning

explanation.surface: A Christmas pudding set alight with smuggled brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'A Smuggler's Song' has 'Brandy for the Parson' among the contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman, who in Kipling's poem receives the smugglers' brandy.

clue.text: Continental articles embrace plan one used to late sun

indicators.note: embrace means hold inside, so one piece is placed within the others

parts.note: la is French for the and der German for the
la is French for the and der German for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: European newspapers welcome a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition: in Lapland, above the Arctic Circle, the sun shines at midnight in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhabitant of the far north, where summer brings the midnight sun.

clue.text: … pour … inn of dish gone to the wall

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as '… pour … inn of dish gone to the wall' is garbled: 'inn of' gives no wordplay for PINUP
annotationWithheld.clue: … pour … inn of dish gone to the wall

clue.text: A slattern retiring in Oklahoma

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: a slattern is a slut, an untidy woman

explanation.surface: An untidy woman retires to Oklahoma.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in the state of Oklahoma.

clue.text: It has to go back on the tenth

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on the second
going back means reading the word backwards

explanation.surface: Something must be returned on the tenth day.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tenth of produce or income given to the church.

clue.text: What is flowery and worn at Epsom inside?

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Flowery hats worn at the Epsom Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, as florid prose is.

clue.text: Quite happy with second things in house?

parts.note: content means satisfied

explanation.surface: Satisfied with the second-hand items in a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessions of a household are insured as such.

clue.text: Luxurious, travelling per bus

indicators.note: travelling suggests movement, so the letters move around

explanation.surface: Luxury travel by bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means magnificent or splendid.

clue.text: Marijuana as smoked in out-. skirts of town-it grows in the tropics

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a reefer is a marijuana cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone smoking cannabis on the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts REEFER between T and N, the first and last letters of 'town'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large tropical fern with a trunk.
